rules.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
rules.description: Extracting files from a malicious ZIP file, or similar type of archive, without validating that the destination file path is within the destination directory can allow an attacker to unexpectedly gain access to resources.
Writing network data directly to the file system allows arbitrary file upload and might indicate a backdoor.
Legacy category for incorrect handling or transformation of structured data.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
rules.description: Directly sending file data in an outbound network request can indicate unauthorized information disclosure.
Accessing paths influenced by users can allow an attacker to access unexpected resources.

rules.cwe_name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
rules.description: Sanitizing an HTTP request parameter may be ineffective if the user controls its type.
A restricted route, URL, script, or file can be requested directly without required authorization.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
rules.description: File access follows a symlink, hardlink, or shortcut to an unintended resource.
Making a network request with user-controlled data in the URL allows for request forgery attacks.
Middleware with case-sensitive paths do not protect endpoints with case-insensitive paths.
